title: Sacred and Profane Love
note: Two women sit at a well — one dressed, one bare — while a child stirs the water between them. The allegory is left unresolved on purpose: the same body shown twice, as thought and as feeling.
source_title: File:Tiziano - Amor Sacro y Amor Profano (Galería Borghese, Roma, 1514).jpg

title: Venus and Mars
note: Mars sleeps while wasps hum about his head and Venus watches, propped and awake. Love here is not an event but a condition — vigilance kept beside oblivion.
source_title: File:Venus and Mars National Gallery.jpg

title: An Allegory with Venus and Cupid
note: Cold, enamelled, almost mineral flesh, with Time and Folly drawing back the curtain. Desire is argued as geometry rather than felt on the skin.
source_title: File:Angelo Bronzino - Venus, Cupid, Folly and Time - National Gallery, London.jpg

title: Primavera
note: Nine figures stand in an orange grove and almost none of them touch. Spring, love and fertility are arranged as a diagram — an argument made out of bodies.
source_title: File:Sandro Botticelli - La Primavera - Google Art Project.jpg

title: Venus of Urbino
note: A goddess installed in an ordinary Venetian bedroom, looking straight out of the picture. The body has become a painted surface first and a person second, which is exactly what makes the gaze so unsettled.
source_title: File:Tiziano - Venere di Urbino - Google Art Project.jpg

title: The Cyclops
note: One enormous eye rises over the hills to look at a sleeping woman. Desire is reduced to a single organ, watching — the most abstract thing a body can do.
source_title: File:Odilon Redon - The Cyclops, c. 1914.jpg

title: The Caress
note: A woman with a cheetah's head rests her cheek against a young man's. Tenderness and predation share one silhouette, and the human face is withheld altogether.
source_title: File:Fernand Khnopff - Caresses - Google Art Project.jpg

title: Jupiter and Semele
note: The god arrives as a wall of gold and flowers, and the mortal dissolves into the ornament that destroys her. Love rendered as architecture.
source_title: File:Jupiter and Semele by Gustave Moreau.jpg

title: The Kiss of the Sphinx
note: The embrace is also an ambush. Two bodies lock into a single dark mass and it is impossible to tell which one is being consumed.
source_title: File:Franz von Stuck - The Kiss of the Sphinx - Google Art Project.jpg

title: The Lovers' Whirlwind, Paolo and Francesca
medium: Graphite, ink and watercolour on paper
note: The adulterous lovers are spun through hell as one vortex of limbs. Blake draws passion as weather — bodies turned into motion rather than flesh.
source_title: File:Blake Dante Hell V.jpg

title: Beata Beatrix
note: Beatrice sits with closed eyes while a red bird drops a white poppy into her hand. Love and death occupy the same still, luminous face.
source_title: File:Dante Gabriel Rossetti - Beata Beatrix, 1864-1870.jpg

title: Mars, Venus, and Cupid
place: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: War disarmed by desire: the god of battle stripped of his armour and reduced to a seated outline, watched by a small winged boy.
source_title: File:Mars, Venus, and Cupid, by Marcantonio Raimondi, 1508, engraving - National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo - DSC08241.JPG

title: Venus Disarming Cupid
note: A few hundred strokes and the whole of a love affair exists: Venus takes Cupid's arrow from him while he twists away. Mannerist drawing at its most abstract, the figure stated as curve and shadow and very little else.
source_title: File:Parmigianino - Venus Disarming Cupid - Google Art Project.jpg

title: Self-Portrait with Saskia
place: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: Rembrandt draws himself and his wife at a tavern table in a few dozen etched lines. Tenderness recorded as a shared glance and a raised glass.
source_title: File:Self-Portrait with Saskia MET DP814514.jpg

title: Paolo and Francesca
medium: Wood engraving for Dante's Inferno, Canto V
note: The two lovers drift in the circle of the lustful, still entwined, weightless and unrepentant. Doré engraves damnation as a texture of light and air.
source_title: File:Gustave Doré - Paolo and Francesca da Rimini.jpg

title: The Kiss (detail)
note: Two bodies cut from a single block, so the embrace is also one mass. The most literal of subjects made the most sculptural.
source_title: File:Le Baiser (detail, Musee Rodin, Paris)-2014-05.jpg

title: Eternal Springtime
note: The figures lean out of the block they were never fully freed from. Movement and tenderness held in the same unfinished gesture.
source_title: File:Eternal Springtime, Auguste Rodin, c. 1886, bronze - Huntington Museum of Art - DSC05255.JPG

title: Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss
note: Cupid's hands and wings are the only support; Psyche's body is weightless, held up by tenderness. Neoclassical marble at its most tender.
source_title: File:Psyché ranimée par le baiser de l'Amour, Louvre.jpg

title: The Waltz
note: Two figures turn until the dress becomes the movement itself. Claudel sculpts the turn rather than the dancers.
source_title: File:Camille Claudel, "La Valse", 1889-1905, bronze fonte (1).jpg

title: The Kiss
medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
note: Two faces are almost lost inside the gold. Klimt buries the human in ornament, and the tenderness survives the pattern.
source_title: File:Klimt - The Kiss.jpg

title: Love
note: A stack of pale, doubled faces, haloed and interchangeable. Love painted as a condition shared rather than a scene observed.
source_title: File:Klimt - Liebe - 1895.jpeg

title: Madonna
note: Love and death share one body, and the halo is also the red halo of pain. The face is bowed into anonymity.
source_title: File:Edvard Munch - Madonna - Google Art Project.jpg

title: The Kiss
note: Two faces merge into a single featureless mass. Munch paints the moment identity stops at the edge of the other person.
source_title: File:Edvard Munch - The Kiss - Google Art Project.jpg

title: The Embrace
note: Bodies drawn as angles and stains, awkward and specific. Schiele keeps every joint human while the colour runs free of the contour.
source_title: File:Egon Schiele - Umarmung (1917).jpg

title: The Dance of Life
note: Three women stand on a summer shore while couples dance behind them: the white of innocence, the red of love, the black of grief. A whole life arranged as one dance.
source_title: File:Edvard Munch - The dance of life (1899-1900).jpg

title: The Birth of Venus
note: Venus arrives on a shell blown in by the winds, and love is staged as a birth rather than a meeting. Botticelli paints desire as weather, flowers and hair, with the body barely touching anything.
source_title: File:Sandro Botticelli 046.jpg

title: Venus with a Mirror
note: The goddess looks at herself while a cupid holds the mirror, and the only love in the picture is self-regard. The body has become a surface being admired, and the admirer is her.
source_title: File:Titian - Venus with a Mirror - Google Art Project.jpg

title: The Garden of Love
note: Rubens gathers his wife, his friends and a fountain of Venus into one garden, and love is described as a social occasion rather than a private one.
source_title: File:El Jardín del Amor (Rubens).jpg

title: The Embarkation for Cythera
note: Lovers set out for the island of Venus, or are returning from it, and nobody can tell which. Love painted as a departure that has already become a memory.
source_title: File:L'Embarquement pour Cythère, by Antoine Watteau, from C2RMF retouched.jpg

title: Mars and Venus United by Love
place: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: Veronese ties the god of war to the goddess with a knot of ribbon while a cupid pulls it tight, and love is literally a knot in the composition.
source_title: File:Mars and Venus United by Love MET DP136513.jpg

title: Ophelia among the Flowers
note: Ophelia floats in a river of flowers with her mouth open, and Redon paints love's grief as a colour rather than an event. The face is almost lost in the blue.
source_title: File:Odilon Redon, Ophelia among the Flowers, The National Gallery, London.jpg

title: The Apparition
note: Salome stands before the head of the man she desired and the vision glows in the air between them. Moreau paints obsession as an apparition, and the body as ornament.
source_title: File:Gustave Moreau A aparição.jpg

title: Love Among the Ruins
note: Two lovers sit among brambles while a figure behind them plays a lute, and love is described as a place rather than a feeling.
source_title: File:Edward Burne-Jones Love Among the Ruins.jpg

title: The Beloved
note: Rossetti crowds the bride with her companions until her face is only one among many, and love is painted as an enclosed garden.
source_title: File:The Beloved D-G-Rossetti-1866.jpg

title: Venus and Cupid in a Niche
place: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: A goddess and a small winged boy stand inside a shell-shaped niche, and love is described by hatching and architecture alone.
source_title: File:Venus and Cupid standing in a niche MET DP854062.jpg

title: The Ill-Assorted Couple
note: An old man and a young woman walk together and exchange a glance that is entirely about money. Dürer engraves a love affair as a transaction, which is one of the most honest images of one.
source_title: File:Albrecht Dürer, The Ill-Assorted Couple, 1495-1496, NGA 6572.jpg

title: Jupiter and Antiope
note: Jupiter approaches the sleeping Antiope in the dark, and the whole of desire is in one raised hand and one shadow. Rembrandt etches seduction as an arrangement of light.
source_title: File:Rembrandt van Rijn, Jupiter og Antiope, 1659, KKS2568, Statens Museum for Kunst.jpg

title: Lovers
medium: Pencil and white chalk on paper
note: Two lovers are drawn as a single line of pencil and chalk with their heads pressed together. The drawing is almost entirely contour, and unmistakably two people.
source_title: File:Gustav Klimt Liebespaar nach rechts c1913.jpg

title: Lovers
note: Schiele draws two bodies as angles and stains, awkward and specific, and the tenderness survives every distortion.
source_title: File:Egon Schiele - Liebespaar - 1913.jpeg

title: The Three Graces
note: Three women stand linked by their arms and shoulders, and the group is one continuous soft curve. Grace described as a single line rather than three bodies.
source_title: File:Canova - The Three Graces, between 1813 and 1816, Н.ск-506.jpg

title: Amor and Psyche
note: Cupid stands with his arm around Psyche and a butterfly resting on his hand, and love is described as a balance between two standing bodies.
source_title: File:Amor en Psyche Sculpturen van Antonio Canova (serietitel), RP-P-OB-39.103.jpg

title: Eros Stringing the Bow
note: The god of love bends his bow and looks up, and the whole of desire is in the tension of one arm. Ancient sculpture at its most abstract and most human.
source_title: File:Eros with Bow, Roman Marble Copy of Bronze Greek Original, c. 2nd C. AD (28309098915).jpg

title: Danaë
note: Danaë curls into a spiral inside a veil of gold with her face almost hidden, and love is painted as a shower of gold rather than as a body.
source_title: File:Klimt - Danae - 1907-08.jpeg

title: Water Serpents
note: Two women embrace in water until their hair and their bodies dissolve into pattern. Klimt paints desire as ornament, and ornament as desire.
source_title: File:Gustav Klimt - Water Serpents II.jpg

title: Vampire (Love and Pain)
note: A woman bends over a man's neck and his face is buried in her hair, and the red hair covers the whole composition. Munch paints love as a wound.
source_title: File:Edvard Munch - Vampire (1893), Munchmuseet.jpg

title: Ashes
note: A woman stands upright in the forest while a man sits with his head in his hands, and the fire between them is already out. Love painted as aftermath.
source_title: File:Edvard Munch - Ashes (1895).jpg
